finding.claim: The OAuth2 `state` value is also used as the authenticated session ID. It is exposed in the IdP redirect URL and in logs, and it is not regenerated after login (session fixation). Anyone who learns or plants the state can use the victim's authenticated session.
finding.source: Attacker obtains or plants the `state` value: an unauthenticated GET /oauth/login?provider=X returns a state and cookie they control. The state also appears in the authorization URL (browser history, Referer, IdP/proxy logs) and in OliveTin Info-level logs. Fixation also needs a way to set the cookie in the victim's browser, e.g. cookie tossing from a sibling subdomain.
finding.sink: CheckUserFromOAuth2Cookie / lookupOAuth2UserByState (lines 409-447) authenticate any request whose `olivetin-sid-oauth` cookie equals a registered state with a populated Username. That user then reaches the ACL-protected API.

trace.note: HandleOAuthLogin generates a 16-byte random state before any authentication
state is registered in registeredStates with an empty Username
the state is set as the httpOnly session cookie `olivetin-sid-oauth`
the state is logged at Info and then sent in the redirect URL to the IdP (line 187)
after the code exchange, the SAME state key is populated with the victim's Username and Usergroup; no new session ID is issued
anyone presenting that state as the cookie value is authenticated as the victim

finding.guards_checked: The callback checks that the cookie equals the query state, which only binds the callback to the browser and does not protect the session ID afterwards. The cookie is HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax. Entries expire after 15 minutes. Nothing rotates the ID after authentication.

finding.claim: The OAuth2 provider config, including ClientSecret, is written to the log at Debug level. The same file logs the OAuth state/session ID (lines 185, 309) and the authorization code (line 312), even though InsecureAllowDump* flags exist for dumps like this.
finding.source: Operator or anyone with read access to logs, log shipping or support bundles, when debug logging is enabled.
finding.sink: log.Debugf("... %+v", providerConfig) writes the config struct, which has the ClientSecret field, to the log output.

trace.note: the ClientSecret is copied into the oauth2.Config, and providerConfig still holds it
the whole providerConfig struct is logged with %+v

finding.guards_checked: No redaction or field filtering. It is not behind an InsecureAllowDump* flag, unlike InsecureAllowDumpOAuth2UserData at line 368. Only the Debug log level gates it.

finding.claim: Argument values are logged in plaintext, including `password`-type arguments. The redaction helpers are only applied to the final command line, not to these per-argument logs.
finding.source: A user submits a password-type argument via StartAction, StartActionAndWait or the exec triggers.
finding.sink: log.WithFields({"name":..., "value": values[arg.Name]}).Debugf("Arg assigned") writes the secret to the logs.

trace.note: logs the raw value for every argument, including arg.Type == "password" (exec path)
the same raw logging in parseActionArguments (shell path)
typeSafetyCheckRegex also logs the rejected value at Warn

finding.guards_checked: redactShellCommand and redactExecArgs only redact the parsed command line (lines 108, 76). They are not applied to the per-argument Debug logs. TypeSafetyCheck accepts password values without any check, so nothing stops them reaching the log.
